candidates.semantic_change: After choosing the existing spatial-middle segment length, compare the span of first-endpoint and last-endpoint projections onto the group direction vector. Keep the endpoint side with the smaller span; ties keep the first endpoint. Paint forward from first endpoints or backward from last endpoints.
candidates.input_general_reason: Endpoint projections and spans use only extracted input cells and the existing segment direction. There is no task-ID branch, fixed color, supplied query answer, or task-specific coordinate. The source direction order, spatial segment ordering and target length remain unchanged.
candidates.tie_break: When both projection spans are equal, keep cells[0] and paint in the original segment direction. This deterministic convention is not tuned to query gold.
candidates.hypothesis_basis: The known demos preserve the aligned endpoint side: horizontal left endpoints, vertical top endpoints, and lower-left diagonal endpoints. The allowed query input introduces diagonal upper-right alignment. This candidate expresses one input-derived common rule across orientations.
limitations: This is a development hypothesis following observation that the earlier frozen query result missed; no query answer was read or used to construct the rule. It is not an untouched confirmation experiment.
Smallest endpoint spread is a heuristic when endpoints are not exactly aligned; equal-spread ambiguity is resolved deterministically, not proved by these demos.
No execution, compilation, model call, or scoring was performed when creating this candidate.
